h1: Cape Town travel, stays & events guide
heroText: Cape Town is South Africa's coastal jewel, wrapped around Table Mountain where a cable car lifts visitors above the city and the Atlantic. First-time visitors should stroll the V&A Waterfront for shops and harbour views, take the ferry to Robben Island for its Nelson Mandela history, and photograph the colourful houses of Bo-Kaap. Cape Town International Airport connects the city to the world, and its mix of mountains, beaches and Cape Winelands makes it one of Africa's top destinations.

areas.name: City Bowl
areas.text: City Bowl is Cape Town's central district beneath Table Mountain, mixing historic architecture, restaurants and the colourful Bo-Kaap quarter.

areas.name: V&A Waterfront
areas.text: The V&A Waterfront combines shopping, harbour-front dining and ferry departures for Robben Island, a convenient base right on the water.

areas.name: Camps Bay
areas.text: Camps Bay lines a palm-fringed Atlantic beach beneath the Twelve Apostles, popular for sundowners and upscale beachfront stays.

areas.name: Sea Point
areas.text: Sea Point's long promenade links the Waterfront to Camps Bay, offering mid-range hotels and easy walking or cycling along the coast.

airports.name: Cape Town International Airport (CPT)
airports.search: Cape Town International Airport, Cape Town, South Africa
airports.text: Cape Town International Airport sits about 20 minutes from the city centre, with buses, shuttles and taxis running regularly to the main hotel districts.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Cape Town International Airport (CPT) and central Cape Town before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in City Bowl or the V&A Waterfront for an easy first stay near Table Mountain, museums and harbour dining, then compare Camps Bay for beach glamour or Sea Point for promenade walks between the two. Each area sits within a short drive of Cape Town's main sights.
hotelIntro: Cape Town hotel choice depends on priorities: City Bowl and the Waterfront suit first-time visitors wanting sights and dining within reach, Camps Bay suits beach-focused stays, and Sea Point suits travelers wanting promenade access at a lower price point.
rentalCars: A rental car is worth having for the Cape Winelands, Cape Point and the Garden Route, though the city centre, Waterfront and Atlantic Seaboard are easily covered by taxi or ride-hailing.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose City Bowl or the V&A Waterfront for an easy first stay close to Table Mountain, museums and harbour restaurants.

travelTips.title: Table Mountain timing
travelTips.text: Book Table Mountain cableway tickets online and go early, since cloud cover and high winds regularly close the cable car.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Use the MyCiTi bus or a pre-booked shuttle from Cape Town International Airport for an easy, affordable ride into the centre.

travelTips.title: Safety awareness
travelTips.text: Keep valuables out of sight in busy areas and use licensed taxis or ride-hailing after dark, as with any major city.

nearbyIdeas.name: Cape Winelands
nearbyIdeas.label: Wine
nearbyIdeas.text: The Cape Winelands towns of Stellenbosch and Franschhoek are under an hour's drive away, ideal for a day of tastings among vineyard-covered valleys.

nearbyIdeas.name: Cape Point
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Cape Point and the Cape of Good Hope anchor a scenic nature reserve at the peninsula's tip, roughly an hour south of the city.

nearbyIdeas.name: Boulders Beach
nearbyIdeas.label: Wildlife
nearbyIdeas.text: Boulders Beach near Simon's Town is home to a colony of African penguins, a popular half-day trip along the False Bay coast.

history.text: In 1497, Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama recorded a sighting of the Cape of Good Hope.

history.label: 16th century
history.text: In the late 16th century French, Danish, Dutch, and English, but mainly Portuguese, ships regularly continued to stop over in Table Bay en route to the Indies.

In 1510, at the Battle of Salt River, the Portuguese admiral Francisco de Almeida and sixty-four of his men were killed and his party was defeated by the "Goringhaiqua" (in Dutch approximate spelling) using.

history.label: 1800s
history.text: The city became the capital of the newly formed Cape Colony, whose territory expanded very substantially through the 1800s, partially as a result of numerous wars with the amaXhosa on the colony's eastern frontier.
The discovery of diamonds in Griqualand West in 1867, and the Witwatersrand Gold Rush in 1886, prompted a flood of immigration into South Africa.

history.label: 1870s
history.text: In 1859 the first railway line was built by the Cape Government Railways and a system of railways rapidly expanded in the 1870s.
In 1895 the city's first public power station, the Graaff Electric Lighting Works, was opened.
Conflicts between the Boer republics in the interior and the British colonial government resulted in the Second Boer War of 1899–1902.
In 1945 the expansion of the Cape Town foreshore was completed, adding an additional 194 ha (480 acres) to the Cape Town CBD, and by extension, the City Bowl region. Apartheid era Prior to.
After it was declared a whites-only area in 1965, all housing there was demolished and over 60,000 residents were forcibly removed.
In 2014 Cape Town was named World Design Capital of the Year.
Cape Town was voted the best tourist destination in Africa at the 2023 World Travel Awards in Dubai and continues to be the most important tourist destination in the country.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: It was later renamed by John II of Portugal as "Cape of Good Hope" (Cabo da Boa Esperança) because of the great optimism engendered by the opening of a sea route to the Indian.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Cape Town became the legislative capital of the Union, and later of the Republic of South Africa.
